1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 948 kWh (88,224 − 87,276), line items sum to $177.83 ($18.79 + $32.97 + $126.07), and the change versus last month is −$42.61 ($177.83 − $220.44); treat any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map both billing periods to the AEP Ohio tariff by date: last month (2026-08-16 to 2026-09-15) and current (2026-09-15 to 2026-10-15) both fall under the post-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.788; tier-1 variable $0.0347738 + $0.13299 = $0.1677638/kWh for the first 2,000 kWh), so there is no rate change and both periods are 30 days, giving price_usd = 0 and days_usd = 0.

3. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 295 / HDD 1.5) to current (CDD 88.5 / HDD 86), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective variable rate, or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

4. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly −$42.61; this captures household usage changes not explained by price, days, or weather (948 vs 1,202 kWh).

5. Check for a billing error: model the current period with the tariff (fixed $18.788 + 948 kWh × $0.1677638 ≈ $177.82) and compare to the actual $177.83; both match within rounding, so billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
